place.title: Tuska
place.summary: Tuska attacked the homeworld of boar-like creatures at some point. These creatures–now referred to as airut–are a proud warrior race, who resort to chaotic, psychological warfare. Many of the Airut joined Tuska due to the strength that she showed. Throughout the years, as the Airut continued to follow Tuska, they became more and more reliant on the symbiotic relationship with the boar god, taking hair dropped by Tuska to form armour and gloves in order to increase their strength. As part of their favour towards psychological warfare, the airut leave the Mark of Tuska stamped on their victims, either as a branding or marks made on the wall. Tuska and the Airut met Skargaroth and Skargaroth followed Tuska through the dimensions to hunt her down.

get_inside.text: South of Falador
The farm is in some ways the crossroads of Asgarnia. It has a convenient location, near Draynor Village, Falador, Port Sarim, and Rimmington. There are several ways to reach the farm.
The fastest way is to utilise the Cabbageport function of the Explorer's ring 3 or 4, as this will teleport the user to the cabbage patch belonging to the farm.
If players have their house in Rimmington, they can teleport to house and run to the farm.
If players have a spirit tree grown in Port Sarim, they can teleport there and run north.
Using the Captain's Log to teleport to Port Sarim and go north.
Teleport to the Port Sarim lodestone and run north, or the Draynor lodestone then run west.
If a player binds their amulet of nature to a patch in the farm, it will teleport the player to the patch when the crops are diseased or fully grown. As this isn't certain, it is rarely used.
Players can charter a ship to Port Sarim and run north.

place.title: Falador farm
place.summary: If that isn't enough, there is also a large pasture containing several cows, which will all drop raw beef, bones, and their prized cowhides. The meat can be cooked in Falador or on a fire to be used as food, the bones buried, and the cowhides tanned and used for Crafting, or sold on the Grand Exchange to others wishing to train Crafting for a fair price. If players don't wish to cook the meat for food, they can also eat the cabbages that spawn in the patch nearby.

• The fastest way is to utilise the Cabbageport function of the Explorer's ring 3 or 4, as this will teleport the user to the cabbage patch belonging to the farm.
• If players have their house in Rimmington, they can teleport to house and run to the farm.
• If players have a spirit tree grown in Port Sarim, they can teleport there and run north.
• Using the Captain's Log to teleport to Port Sarim and go north.
• Teleport to the Port Sarim lodestone and run north, or the Draynor lodestone then run west.
• If a player binds their amulet of nature to a patch in the farm, it will teleport the player to the patch when the crops are diseased or fully grown. As this isn't certain, it is rarely used.
• Players can charter a ship to Port Sarim and run north.

get_inside.text: Lunar Sea

The Pirates' Cove can be accessed only by boat. Players may reach the island either by the 'Travel-Pirates' Cove' option on Lokar Searunner in Rellekka or by the 'Travel' option on Captain Bentley on Lunar Isle, provided they have reached a certain point in Lunar Diplomacy. There is no fee either way.

There are no teleportation methods through which a player can immediately reach the island; however, players may reach the Lady Zays port of call on Lunar Isle more quickly by using the Lunar Isle lodestone or the Moonclan Teleport found in the lunar spells, which is a reward for the Lunar Diplomacy quest. Players can also access Rellekka more quickly through a variety of means, including the enchanted lyre or House Teleport spell (provided their player-owned house is in Rellekka).

place.title: Pirates' Cove

get_inside.text: Wilderness
While there is no direct teleport to the Pirates' Hideout, there are a couple of relatively safe routes to take as the area is not often travelled by player killers.
Using Slayer cape or Master slayer cape the player can teleport to Mandrith who is directly east of the Pirate's hideout.
Using Wilderness sword 4 player can teleport directly to the Wilderness Agility Course and then can travel east to the hideout.

Using the Edgeville-Wilderness lever or the Ardougne-Wilderness lever to teleport to the Deserted Keep east of the Mage Arena. After cutting the spider web blocking the top of the exit from Deserted Keep, run west past the Mage Arena until you reach the hideout. In the past this was a popular player killing location so many players would run south of the Mage Arena and swing back north to the hideout which took longer. However, these days the route is fairly safe.

Players who have completed Desert Treasure may use the Ghorrock Teleport to the Ice Plateau and run north through the gate and then east past the Wilderness Agility Course and then north to reach the hideout. Beware that this route will drop you directly into an area with aggressive Greater Demon Berserkers, and the route will take you past aggressive Wyverns and Glacors.

place.title: Wise Old Man's house
place.summary: The house was owned by him many years ago, but was left to an old girlfriend Zenevivia after they fought and he left her to go adventuring. She took the house and changed it so that it was very advanced. During the events of Love Story, the Wise Old Man and the player return to the house in response to a challenge by Zenevivia to a duel. After getting past traps and monsters, the player gets to Zenevivia, fights her, then wins. After the events of Love Story, the Wise Old Man regains ownership, however players do not have access to the house after the quest, but they can make their house the same style this house is in. The Wise Old Man decided to leave this house because it contained too many bad memories.

The player-owned houses (often shortened to POH) are personal, customisable houses that the players can build with the Construction skill following the completion of There's No Place Like Home.... They are located in the instanced pocket dimension accessible through the house portals in several locations. Houses can consist of up to 25 rooms of various shapes and sizes, which can be filled with up to 500 pieces of furniture. Furniture is created on the furniture workbench in Rimmington, stored in the nearby furniture storage, and then freely placed anywhere on the player's plot of land, both inside and outside. The plot is square-shaped with a side length of 48 game squares for a total of 2,304 usable game squares. Rooms can be flexibly assembled in to one or more buildings and furniture can be freely moved and rotated in build mode.

get_inside.text: The Living Rock Caverns are found below the dwarven mines beneath Ice Mountain, near Falador.
Dungeoneering cape teleport to the Dwarven Mine resource dungeon and then running north and west to the cavern entrance.
Through a directed skill portal in the Max Guild of Prifddinas. Requires Plague's End and at least one 99 or a Quest Cape.

The Lassar Teleport from the Ancient Magicks spellbook, the Edgeville Monastery teleport from the combat bracelet, or the Body altar teleport all teleport close to this entrance of the Dwarven Mine. Then run south to the cavern entrance.
Through the entrance in the north-east corner of Falador or the Mining Guild and then run north and then west to the entrance to the Living Rock Caverns.

Take the mine cart from Keldagrim to Ice Mountain. From the cart station, go south to the second passage way east. From here, first go east and then north around a chasm. At the top end of this chasm, climb a rope down to the Living Rock Caverns. Players can also travel to the Grand Exchange and White Wolf Mountain on the mine cart system, as well as Dorgesh-Kaan through the Dorgesh-Kaan–Keldagrim train system (if the player has completed Another Slice of H.A.M.). Jagex has also pointed out that players can smelt and smith their ore at the Blast Furnace near the cart station in Keldagrim.
Using the scan option on the Disk of returning (Gower Quest) and then returning using the scan option again. Run north east to the Living Rock Caverns entrance.

Agility course

Teleports

Anachronia Teleport spell if a Totem of the Abyss is planted and active
Anachronia tablet to teleport to the Player Lodge; it requires the Love Story quest and a tier 2 Player Lodge
Ancient seed to Herby Werby
Mystical tree in two steps: Manor Farm to Anachronia Dinosaur Farm (or Anachronia Dinosaur Farm teleport) and then run south-east; use a tree again to reach the west coast of Anachronia

The God Wars Dungeon (often abbreviated as GWD), originally known as the Temple of Lost Ancients, is a dangerous dungeon where armies of various gods, left over from the God Wars, fight one another to the death. Its release was announced in the Behind the Scenes of August 2007.

• They will need to battle other people and monsters. Higher combat levels would be advantageous, but they are not absolutely necessary.

get_inside.text: The entrance to the dungeon is located east of the pulley, which is used to enter Senntisten behind the Ancient door just north of the Archaeology Guild.
Use the boss portal in War's Retreat.
Use the boss portal in the Max Guild (requires 99 in every skill).
Use the Pontifex Shadow Ring, restored after the City of Senntisten quest, to teleport to Senntisten, run north to the Pulley.

Use the Archaeology journal to teleport to the Archaeology Guild, then walk north to the ancient door (dungeon), east to the ancient doors (The Empty Throne Room) or north-east to a winch (Senntisten Temple).
Using a gnome glider to fly to Lemanto Andra (3) leaves the player very close to the ancient door.

The dig sites map in the Archaeology Guild, archaeology teleport or the master archaeologist's outfit can be used to teleport to the Senntisten Dig Site camp just north-east of the cathedral, provided the player has level 60 Archaeology or access to those items.
Dig site pendant can be used to teleport to the following:
Varrock Dig Site - Archaeologist's workbench & Bank chest, walk north-west to the ancient door.
Senntisten Temple - north-west winch entrance to temple.
Skeletal horror Teleport or invitation box can be used to teleport to the north-east of the ancient door.
Teleport to Earth altar, or using Fort Forinthry Teleport to the north-west of the ancient door.
Ride the balloon to Varrock to the north-west of the ancient door.

Use the Ring of kinship to teleport to Daemonheim, and then run east to the treasure chest. Use the teleport on the chest and select The Zamorakian Undercity (requires completion of Impressing the Locals).
Use the teleport on the treasure chest outside Temple of Aminishi, The Shadow Reef, or the Dragonkin Laboratory (requires completion of Impressing the Locals).

place.title: The Zamorakian Undercity
place.summary: While it is considered an Elite Dungeon (with its own luck charms and ability to teleport to the other Elite Dungeons) it is noticeably different compared to the previous three; the health of enemies scales to the party size (and are also more dangerous) and its luck charm costs slightly more and cannot be converted. It also possesses an enrage system that goes up in intervals of 100% past 4,000% enrage, and the enemies' strengths, types, and quantities begin to change as it increases, capping at 60,000%. Players are free to choose their enrage from 0 to 4,000%. Clearing the undercity increases the rewards obtained from Zamorak.
